review:
This game genuinely makes me happy. 

The devs succeeded in creating a really atmospheric puzzle game. The music really mellows you out, and the artwork is fitting extremely well done; simple but elegant. The puzzles come in all shapes and sizes with a few minigames for variety's sake. They arent easy enough to make the game boring, nor are they impossible because of the game's voluntary hint system (which I think is clever). Even the one or two hard puzzles that you can't use hints on (I'm looking at you world map) are beatable if you rack your brain a bit and give you a pleasant sense of accomplishment. Its a game that one would enjoy playing between games, something to relax and fall in to after a disasterous game of league, doto, or cs. 

My only complaint is that this game is too short and that I'm going to miss it when I finish it :c

[b]Short Version:[/b]
[list]
    [*]Recommended, but only if on sale, and mainly for the great art.
    [*]Seasoned P&C/HOG players will not be impressed by gameplay.
    [*]If you're colorblind, skip this altogether - the minigames rely too much on color-matching.
[/list]

[b]PROS:[/b]
+ Beautiful art
+ Nice soundtrack
+ Smooth mechanics
+ Some unique puzzles

[b]CONS:[/b]
- No real story
- Repetitive tasks
- No instructions for puzzles/minigames
- No choice to skip puzzles/minigames
- Includes 2 short but stressful 8-bit 'obstacle-avoidance' action minigames (not what P&Cers are looking to play)
- Hint system not very good
- Anticlimactic and unsatisfying "ending" (if it can be called one)
- No replay value.
__________________________________

[b]Long Version:[/b]
My feelings towards this game are mixed. I bought it based on all the positive reviews, and while I did enjoy it (mostly), and I do recommend the game (on sale), I still have a bunch of curmudgeonly gripes.

[u][b]STORY[/b][/u]
It didn't feel like there was much of a story. The wordless intro clip only show a basic scenario: meteor hits planet, planet breaks into puzzle pieces, you need to find them all and fix the planet. Not much of a plotline, just an excuse for the player to do stuff. The store description says that the world "fell apart" and "its future depends on you", but I honestly expected a bit more for the main objective than [i]literally[/i] putting a picture puzzle back together. And aside from the puzzle pieces, the actual game feels disconnected from the initial "story" idea; it doesn't seem like there's any dire trouble to tackle in the world - just finding misplaced parts and accessing new areas. There's not much that connects the minigames, puzzles, and hidden object bits to an actual story, anyway. Yes, the puzzle pieces fix the planet. But how does anything else in the game itself factor into the "story"? I know that's being nitpicky, but if "Story" is in your title, there should at least be more plot-like connections between the tasks a player must complete.

[u][b]GAMEPLAY[/b][/u]
You get a couple of initial tutorial arrows showing what to click on, but then you're on your own. The puzzle piece hunt is obvious, but you still have to click around to find out what parts of the scene need "fixing". Those bits give you an secondary objective to find a certain number of objects (gears, pipes, dice, etc) to fix the broken part. Sort of a semi-hidden-object hunt. After fixing your ladder/panel/door/whatever, you either unlock another area, or are presented with a minigame/puzzle to complete in order to get the last piece for [i]another[/i] secondary objective. Basically, "Find all the _____, or else you'll never get that last _____." At least clicks are precise, and the movement between scenes/areas is very fluid.

[u][b]MINIGAMES/PUZZLES[/b][/u]
Many of the puzzles were very familiar/common in other games. But there are a handful I haven't seen in P&Cs/HoGs before, and the difficulty varied, which was nice. Either way, you get NO instructions once you start. Some are intuitive - like the "Simon Says" levers, or a version of that tube puzzle where you rotate pipes to complete a network. But many have you scratching your head before you realize what you're supposed to be doing in the first place. (I spent far too long on the Compass "puzzle" until I looked up the solution out of frustration.) At least you can click the red X to exit and reset everything if you mess up.

I [i]really[/i] didn't like the action 'video game' minigames you're forced to play to continue, and was very glad there were only two. They're 8-bit obstacle games: one guiding a boat up and down to avoid walls, and one moving a plane left and right to avoid trees and planes. If you crash even once, you start over. They're not all that difficult, but they introduce an unwelcome level of stress that I generally play P&Cs/HoGs to [i]avoid[/i]. 

Oh, and forget about finishing the game if you get stuck. You can't skip a single thing. Not cool.

[u][b]HINT SYSTEM[/b][/u]
The hint system is cute, but iffy. Click on the blue flies to fill the "?" meter. Once it's full and clicked, a red bug will fly out and circle around whatever you're supposed to click or focus on next. The problem is that if you're in the wrong scene within a level, the bug will simply fly to the edge of the screen to the signpost arrow. I understand that means the next 'piece' or whatever is not in the current scene, but when you move to the next scene the bug disappears. So all you really got as a hint was "Nope, it's not here". Then the hint bar won't release a bug again for quite a while, even when full. I don't know what the timer is on it, but it's annoying to unknowingly "waste" hints like that. It's not difficult to refill the meter, but that really doesn't do much good if you can't use it.

[u][b]VARIETY[/b][/u]
The description calls each chapter "vastly different". I disagree with most of that. Different, somewhat. Vastly, no. Any major differences between levels are purely cosmetic. It's just different scenes, music, and what type of objects you need to find. The minigames/puzzles themselves are obviously going to be different, but that's expected for any game like this, so I wouldn't consider that a "vast" difference. 
The tasks in each level are pretty much the same: 
1) Find all the hidden puzzle pieces.
2) Find multiple objects to "fix" things so you can progress. Objects are hidden in similar ways in each level (behind panels, overlaying a similar shape, blending into the background, etc).
3) Help some random person (usually just a version of "find this many ____").
4) Solve a handful of minigames or puzzles.
5) Put the puzzle pieces together at the end of each level.
That said, it didn't take long for it to feel a little repetitive. 

[u][b]ENDING[/b][/u]
[i]What[/i] ending? [spoiler]When you complete the world puzzle, you're put in a room with the people you helped out. Initially you think it's a bonus level, but then you realize all you can do is change the radio to play music from each level, and in the next room you can replay each minigame/puzzle individually. Beyond that...what exactly was accomplished?[/spoiler] It's very anticlimactic and unfulfilling.

[u][b]REPLAY VALUE[/b][/u]
None whatsoever. You can't complete a level if you don't find/solve everything, so once you play through, you're done. [i]Maybe[/i] it has replay value if you want to revisit a minigame. But I don't see myself loading this up again just to play a puzzle with a 1-minute-or-less solution.

[u][b]CONCLUSION[/b][/u]
Despite my nitpicking, I do recommend the game to PoC/HoG fans (wait for a sale though - save the $5 for a latte or something). The lovely art and music are worth a look, at the very least. If the game was any more expensive, I'd probably just go look at some nice galleries on deviantART instead. But honestly I can't comment/complain about value, since I got it on sale for $0.49.

This is the game I'm playing before going to bed, generally in 30 mins sessions. 
Everything is so relaxing, peaceful and gently colorful, that it helps me to unwind after a long day of work.

One of the best puzzle games I ever played. Love the art (which is handdrawn). Refreshing that it has no text at all and is good for all ages.

It's very pretty, and it starts out strong, but tedium and repetiition set in when each chapter repeats the theme of finding an array of hidden objects to first reassemble and then work your way through proper puzzles, with a few reflex tests thrown in on a few occasions. Each chapter ends with you literally putting the tiny world back together with twenty-five (!) puzzle pieces painstakingly found in the last world. Unfortunately a good third of the jigsaw is lightly cloudy or starry space, which makes many of the sky pieces nearly identical to a glance.
There's a built-in puzzle-spotter, which is obnoxious. To charge it for a single activation, you have to click thirty (30!) small, flying insects, which is simply punitive. There are also 'solutions' available for each puzzle, but be aware that many are reversed, incomplete, or actually wrong.
The game has maybe two hours worth of play. A tiny amount of time for a tiny bang, I suppose.

Apart from that, the puzzles are mostly very good, the art design is hand drawn and absolutely cute, the soundtrack fits extremely well and then there's again a minor flaw with some very few hidden items being close to impossible to find without the hint system.

All in all it's a neat 3-4 hours playthrough and worth the asking price in my opinion.

Sadly, I cannot recommend the game. It looks like a fun puzzle game to relax and enjoy, but the game has multiple issues where puzzles do not work. I went to a guide to see what I was doing wrong, only minutes in the game, and found it is touch and go if the game works on your system. My guess, it is dated and no longer working well on newer systems.

Just as well, when you go to full screen, you get only a corner of the game showing on the top left of the screen. The game in windowed cannot have the resolution changed. There are not really much in the way of options. Additionally, the mouse clicks do not always register precisely. This led me to check if I had something setup wrong, and found this is a common issue. 

In short, the game might be problematic on newer computers. As such, I cannot recommend it as I cannot get past the game breaking issues.

I played this with my kids, aged 7 and 5, and it was lovely.

It's basically a hidden object game.  There's little in the way of story, it's just a collection of puzzles and a jigsaw minigame.  Saying that, though, reduces it too far.  The gentle music, the lovely artwork and charming depictions of the people and puzzles all combine together to make a lovely, relaxing little game.

In general, the 5yo enjoyed looking for all the puzzle pieces, which are cunningly hidden like "where's wally" in the artwork.  The 7yo enjoyed trying to solve the puzzles themselves, while daddy (47yo) was there to explain what some things were, and try to keep the other two guided to look in the right places.

The game took about 10 hours to play, but generally because I left the kids to it.  The puzzles are usually not too hard, although there are a few that need quite a bit of puzzling through.  The hidden-object part of the game is usually not too bad, but there are some items which are hidden in very hard-to-see places unless you have a really good monitor.  We tried to play it on the TV through Steamlink, and you needed to get right up to the TV to see some things  occasionally.

We really loved this game, and my 5yo keeps asking if we can play it again from scratch :)

The graphics and drawing is calm and cool, kind of retro cartoon. Its a good game for a laid back casual feel and easy pace, puzzles are not too hard. I do wish they would do a sequel or release a game with similar feel and shape. You have several parts of the world to complete with fun area's a beautiful drawings.

I enjoyed this game greatly. I'm not good at action, shoot'em-up games, preferring puzzles and strategy games that help my brain (I've had a stroke), and this game was perfect. I struggled with the 'boat going through the channels' and the 'flying simulator' games, but overall, I really loved playing this game. Also, the artwork is lovely.

Would have liked a bit of a story tie in, backstory or something. Took me about 5 hours to complete, some of the puzzles will challange you others you will finish in seconds. Worth getting it on 50% or higher rebate, personally I recommend waiting until a 75% off special comes around.

Good for the price, with really nice artwork.   There are however, some action mini-games that require careful timing and can't be skipped.  So that prevents some people from progressing.  Not worth buying if you can't get through the mini-games.  I didn't find them too bad but they weren't fun either.  The rest is ok, though some puzzles require trial and error to determine what combination is the desired endpoint.  Some of its kind of random, though none of the puzzles are too terribly difficult. I ended up using a walkthrough for some of the hidden object elements and to avoid the trial and error of having to find out what was expected, but not for the actual sequences needed to solve the puzzle.  The exception was the compass puzzle, which was honestly terrible.  If you get to it just turn the compass 3 times counter-clockwise and save yourself a headache.  Puzzle-wise it's not really equal to Machinarium but it is good overall, a nice game to relax with, mostly.

I really liked this game! Very relaxing. Simple but not too much childish. The game is really kind and helps you a lot.
Warning anyway: there are some riddles with colors, that may be difficult for some people. 
Don't worry if you miss some jigsaw pieces into a chapter: you will be able to succeed anyway :) 
It's a really pleasant point and click game, with nice drawings and ambience.

This game is very special to me as it's the first game I ever played. My dad brought home what would be the family desktop one day and downloaded it through the ColibriGames site for me and my brother before it was even put on Steam. Without it, I'm not sure gaming as a whole would've captured me the way it has since then, so I hold the experience it gave me close to my heart.

Rose-tinted glasses aside, upon my recent reply, this game is still just as good as it was when I first played it. It's not a very long game, but it gives you what you came for: A relaxing point-and-click puzzle game with a gorgeous artstyle and soundtrack. The art is textbook 2000's, with all the wonky proportions, the vibrancy of the colors, and overall expressiveness that's become more and more rare these days; the product of a better time on the internet. What's always amazed me is how it doesn't feel dated at all. Having everything hand-drawn with little movement to throw things off keeps it just this nice bundle of art with the little bits of interactive changes. It's insanely charming and is always a joy to look at while solving the puzzles.

The puzzles themselves are pretty good as well for what they are. A lot of them are particularly tricky as they have really vague completion requirements, but I prefer that over them being breezy and letting you blow past the levels. There's no dialogue or text whatsoever besides grunts from the NPC's, and a hint system, having you collect a certain amount of (what seem like) dragonflies to unlock a pointer to an item you missed. It's very basic but that's all you need in a game like this. Personally, I love the lack of dialogue as it let's me relax and immerse with the music and maintains the feeling of complete serenity throughout each section.

This game is perfect if you just want something to sit down with for an hour or two, do a handful of puzzles and really wind down and immerse yourself in something for a bit. It's not abundant in terms of length, plot or gameplay, but that's it's strength as it offers more than enough for what it is.
I love this game! It took me about 5 hours to play through, and a couple of the puzzles had me stumped for a bit.  Overall a beautiful, peaceful and charming game.
Played with my 6 year old grandson. He absolutely loved the game and was sad when we finished it.

Cute and colorful, but seems that it could have been much more intuitive.
Searching for items is sometimes tedious, and clicking randomly sometimes gets the job done.  Some of the puzzles make no sense for why they are what they are.  I had to consult guides for completing several of the finding parts puzzles, as well as code puzzles.  The number puzzle in the first part made no sense for why the code was what it was.  I saw the parts that gave the information, but it had no obvious reasoning for why the numbers were the ones they were.

[b]Deduction, logic, observation, luck... If you like puzzle games that require some thinking without, however, needing an engineer degree, this game is for you.[/b]

The Tiny Bang Story is a short (4-5 hours) yet stimulating game in which you have to find hidden objects and solve puzzles. There is no story at all, so don't expect a Point & Click adventure - or any BANG for that matter. Even if most of the puzzles are indeed accessible, some will require more time, patience and... a functional brain !

The gameplay is quite simple and intuitive ; navigate through the areas, collect items, unlock puzzles, find what's missing, solve puzzles, unlock more areas, etc. If at some point you don't know what to do and are out of ideas, there's a hint button to prevent despair. Let's not forget to mention the gorgeous and colourful hand-drawn artwork and the relaxing soundtrack that make the playing experience so much more enjoyable.

I would recommend the Tiny Bang Story if you're looking for an average puzzle solving game to lighten up, take up the challenge, or just to kill time, because it's a cute and refreshing adventure.

Excellent game - mostly relaxing (with a few annoying/difficult puzzles). If you like hidden object puzzle games, this one is a must, as it's different from usual hidden object games. 

It's not TOO long, I'm currently on my third play through with just over 15 hours, so it's up to you if you want to pay full price, although I'd still argue that it's worth it. If you see it on sale, definitly get it!

fun 3 hour game. great art and relaxing music. Some puzzles do not make sense at all. Needed youtube guides to solve like 2 stupid puzzles. buy when on sale.

It's not what I expected it to be. I like the graphics, music and the theme of restoring a planet and helping its inhabitants. 

However the game falls short of "Use your imagination and creativity"  statement found in the description. It is a mindless clickfest of every pixel on a tiny screen in order to progress.  Some elements are so small I would never notice them if I didn't accidentally click them.

A gorgeous and somewhat challenging hidden-object game, with several nice puzzles and a few simple mini-games.

Well, I recommend it, but keep your expectations low. There is no story and no point-and-click adventuring: your only task is to find all the objects, and they are quite hard to find indeed! Supposedly you need to collect all the puzzle pieces, but I did not and still completed the game.

If you've enjoyed the audio-visual style here, I strongly recommend Amanita Design's games--Machinarium, Botanicula--which offer wonderful stories and much more gameplay.

If you've enjoyed the gameplay here, well, "hidden-object games" is a huge genre. There are many excellent "HOGs" on Steam. Welcome aboard!

Finally, I'd like to thank the developer for supporting Linux.

It was okay, I guess. If I had the chance to buy it again, knowing what I know now, I would not... and it was only $1 or something.

[spoiler]Did not care for the compass puzzle as there was no hint (that I could find anyway), that suggested rotating counter-clockwise[/spoiler]. I had to look it up after spending way too much time on it and getting nowhere. [spoiler]The puzzle pieces are pointless, as they are just given to you at the end of a chapter whether you find them all or not.[/spoiler] [spoiler]The fountain puzzle was not intuitive, I just randomly moved things around until something worked.[/spoiler] I still have no idea what I was supposed to be trying to accomplish. And big note for the devs, here... Those arcade games are the absolute worst. They aren't puzzles, clicking the mouse on arrow buttons on screen to move is dumb as heck, especially when there is a third button to hit way off to the other side for whatever reason... that stuff doesn't belong in a puzzle/hidden object game.

A brain-aching concoction of point-and-click puzzle and hidden-object genres, [i]The Tiny Bang Story[/i] invites you to save its post-apocalypse surreal world with clickity-clickety-clicks, clicks, clicks, and clicks (I have to admit that in the late game I just went clicking like mad, no brain).  

You will be asked to find designated objects strewn all over the places and, upon having found them all, the puzzle minigame will be unlocked. I love that hidden-object aspect of the game, but the puzzles were quite... various and enjoyable. Okay. But there are some puzzles which you probably won't know what to do with it actually. Many you can experiment and will finally figure it out. But what if you can't? And since this game suffers the serious lack of clue (and we players, with it), you will be forced to resort to view the puzzle solution. And with no explanation whatsoever still. Also, there was this specific one in which the game control was the worst I did wonder how they could release the game without fixing it, and not even an update to solve the issue. And that [i]color-coded world map puzzle[/i]. Vexed and bordering on despair, yet too obstinate to yield and view the solution, I just randomly clicked it until it solved itself. Pretty funny when you put it that way. But, yeah, some puzzles were simply too much and did offset all the fun, the amount of which was not that great in the first place.

While I did enjoy parts of the game and don't feel ripped off since I only spent $1 or less on it, I still can't recommend it. It's a cheap imitation of an Amanita game, reminding me of Samorost, and Machinarium in particular with the pixel hunting, completely out of place action minigames and at least one puzzle that made me want to kick the developer's dog. Unfortunately, unlike Samorost or Machinarium, there's no story or likeable characters, and the "difficulty" spikes too often.

[h1]The Good[/h1]
+Bright, colorful artwork.

+Very relaxing music. You'll have to Google a download for it since the original free posting of music is now a dead link.

[h1]YMMV[/h1]
~Between 3-5 hours of play, depending on how often you look at a guide because you're tired of the game's bullcrap.

~4:3 aspect ratio and small resolution. Not a big deal at all, but it'll make someone whinge, I'm sure.

~There is a hint system for finding objects, but it requires clicking on a large number of ever-present dragonflies to "charge up". It's baffling design and isn't any help with puzzles.

[h1]The Bad[/h1]
-45 seconds to load a glorified DOS game into a usable menu? I can boot all of 2016's Doom faster - and that's got half a dozen unskippable opening splash screens!

-Moments of extreme pixel hunting; not just to find an object, but to successfully click on it.

-The puzzle items on the right side of the screen can block the game environment

-Puzzle pieces are bugged or pointless. You can complete levels without enough, and in one case, too many somehow.

-No ability to skip puzzles and you're going to want to pass on a few due to lacking feedback, or their being a choice between a ton of trial and error or major brainstorming that doesn't fit how casual the rest of the game is.

-No ability to skip that second stupid Colibrivision minigame. Tiger handheld games weren't fun for this crap in the 80's and they're not fun now in an otherwise ostensibly casual puzzle game. Machinarium tried this years prior and got flamed for it...why would you imitate the second worst part of that game?

-Can't exit from the intermission jigsaw puzzle sections until completed, and half the pieces are nondescript blue sky.

This is a calm, relaxing, hidden object game with little puzzles included in each level. Some puzzles present more challenge than others, obviously the further into the game you get the harder the puzzle. It's not a long game but you won't feel ripped off for $5. No worries if you can't find a hidden object, the flies will help you. There is also an interesting little story to the game if you're paying attention. Nothing deep, just a little history of the townsfolk. Definitrly recommended for those looking for something casual and relaxing.

Cute game with nice graphics but avoid it if you suffer any significant colour-blindness because you'll probably find some of the puzzles impossible to complete. Too many of them rely on tiny shade differences and there's no workaround or skip option so you'll just get stuck without help. Beware.

- The hints for some puzzles are sometimes not much instructive
-  The indicator still shows I missed some puzzle pieces although I already collected them all. I had to check the Internet to prove that I got them all. 

Conclusion: Despite the little bugs, it is still functioning, fun games. Definitely worth the money!

I didn't know the art was stolen, if I knew I wouldn't have bought this game.
It's quite pretty, and good for people who just want to relax and kill time, which is not my case. I'm not a "point-and-click game" kind of person, but I got it for the art... and then I found it was stolen. Bummer.

This game is a cute point and click, mostly hunting for objects. It's relaxing and passes the time and I was reasonably entertained. But you need to complete games-within-the-game to advance, and it isn't just one of them. I stopped playing after a while (probably about 60% of the way through) because it was too annoying to have to play the surprisingly long arcade games. I don't particularly recommend it for that reason.

Tiny story indeed. A soccer ball hits the world and turns it into a jigsaw puzzle. There's your story. The ending is even worse. 

Of course it has somewhat of an excuse: it's a very casual hidden object game; lots of tiny things to click on, pretty art set at a relatively tiny (but acceptable) box resolution and a tiny amount of options/configuration.

You're thrown into a scene of half a dozen screens or so and left to click on things for goals to pop up, usually to find X amount of other things to progress or solve a puzzle. There are several areas and maybe 25-30 explorable screens total, not counting puzzle screens. You also find jigsaw pieces throughout and piece some of your world back together on the title screen after each major area.

There are sliding, jigsaw and pipe puzzles and other minor brainteasers. The best thing I can say about the game is it looks very nice and is charming, the worst that it leaves you feeling you accomplished very little, if anything at all.

I love the art style of this game, and even 14 years after the release it really stands the test of time.

There are only 5 levels of finding items and fitting them into a variety of classic puzzles, which makes for a very short game, but at £0.85 it is a good value for money ratio.

There are frustrating moments where the clues are not helpful, some items fail to trigger on click (not sure if it was a bug) and it has a peculiarity to open in a small windowed mode, with a workaround provided in a form of a full-screen button toggle in the top right.

If you enjoy classic puzzles and hand-drawn artwork you'll find this game a delightful diversion, especially if bought on deep discount.
Awesome Point&Click game, its more like a collectable point&click game, but it is really good!

Good HOG game, short and sweet. Art style is nice, reminiscent of games by Amanita Design. Great music too. Well worth the price IMO.

There are some negatives though. They weren't enough to sour my experience, but YMMV:
[list]
[*]Story is non-existent with no indication of your motivation, or even who you are.
[*]The hint system is annoying, and doesn't help you if the thing you need is behind an interaction (eg. opening a pot). Also, the hints tend to give the solution away, when what you really want is just a clue.
[*]Some of the puzzles felt out of place (the boat and plane ones), requiring quick responses and mouse positioning in a game where you normally play at your own pace. I'm a diverse gamer so they were more frustrating than hard for me, but they might be too challenging for people who mainly play HOGs.
[/list]
IMPORTANT: If you have a custom scaling in your Display Options, change it back to 100%, otherwise your cursor won't be visible in full screen.

As a fan of point-and-click adventures, I really wanted to enjoy The Tiny Bang Story. Unfortunately, the puzzles became tedious, the gameplay felt boring, and I quickly lost interest. Not recommended.

It is a hidden object game with some light puzzles. Looks alright. But I'm giving it a thumbs down, because technical issues and sketchy approach to art (no pun intended).

I played this game in the past on a different platform, didn't have issues. But playing it now on Steam I ran into game breaking bug. There was some silly crashing for me as well, but I found a solution on Steam forums, turns out at some point the game would crash if the sound is turned off. Should've been fixed by now, but it's not. Regarding the game breaking bug, looks like it might happen to anyone due to the way the game counts objects you need to find. It is possible to collect something, but the counter will not increase and you'll be effectively locked out of the progress further. No chapter replay or reset is provided, so the only way to dealing with such bug is replaying from the very beginning.

And as for the art, [url=https://artsammich.blogspot.com/2011/05/good-artists-borrow-great-artists-steal.html]apparently[/url] the game artist is quite frivolous with using other artists' works as references, and basically steals parts of their pieces.

Overall it feels like an attempt to cash in on Machinarium audience with somewhat dumbed down gameplay (hidden object instead of point-and-click adventure, although it still has mini-puzzles and mini-games). A fairly successful attempt at the time, I assume, despite the questionable choices of the artist. But a dated attempt as of today, mainly because of unaddressed technical issues.

Such beautiful and calm puzzle game! Music, art, puzzle difficulty, thankful for the ability of hints too in the form of cute critters :) That "click" sound when picking the puzzle pieces was just that perfect little detail for me! Absolutely recommended.

Some kind of issues with being able to use the game in full screen mode.  Although there appears to be an option for full screen, it is displayed as a window, which is both distracting and almost impossible to see often tiny icons, etc. that the player is meant to be looking for.  Clincher for me was the flaky 8 bit battleship thingy in the second chapter.  Due to tremor issues I can't deal with platform/tetris type puzzles.  Way too challenging for me and not in a good way.  Like frustration?  Give this a whirl!

I originally got this game for around 50p with a coupon I got a while back and I've only just been bothered to play it. I expected it to be something that wasn't really for me but after playing it, I'm so glad I bought it.
It's a nice little puzzle game, that's not too hard yet it's not too easy either. The music fits really well with it and it's really quite relaxing to play. 
I think the only criticism I have about this game is that it's a little bit too short for £3.99, I would have liked to see a few more levels.
7/10

If you don't, there's enough backtracking and minute pointless nonsense to turn you off before you get far.  It's an indy game, it's not big, it's unfair to levy high expectations.  Still, the measure of a game is whether you're having fun or not.  I'm in the category of folks who is annoyed by pixel hunts and doesn't care for nonsensical puzzles (good-bye, most adventure games).  So ask yourself what you enjoy, and it'll let you know whether this is your sort of game.

A nice relaxing mini puzzles game with soothing music and artwork combined between surrealism and whimsical (picture book/storybook style).

The puzzles are a bit too "clean" imo... which makes them pretty easy to solve/predict. But it's still great enough for casual puzzle lover or beginners to enjoy.

Love the music, they're good enough to keep the game on just to listen to them. (There's a music player at the end of the game that let you listen to all of them.)

This story game uses seek and find (then click), then solve puzzles with the pieces you found, to show you a story.  The art style  is cute but not cloyingly so.  The music is good, and didn't become so discracting that I shut it off.  I laughed out  loud at the silliness of some of elements in the various "chapters".  The puzzles are all different, and have some rather clever twists to puzzles that puzzler afficianados will appreciate.   This game doesn't have achievements, which this game doesn't need.  If you finished that game without cheats/guides, THAT is an achievement.

It's a cutesey hidden object adventure, casual, brief, time killer.  It's about 3 ish hours long. Recommended especially right now,as it's being offered for free or when it's on sale (As I did several months ago) after that offer expires.

One huge caveat though. There is a game killing bug - that has been solved by the excellent community NOT the devs (Which is not cool, reallydevs. tbh). If on the last real exploratory area you have the sound muted for any reason (The musics pretty decent, though) and attempt to enter the final area the game will hard crash every time. i had two virtually complete goes at it including an uninstall before finding that solution.

Replay value is limited, as it's really only the mini games from the final area that you can do again, without replaying the whole thing. It's doesn't vary so once solved it's kind of done. Despite that it's not a time spent I regret so I'd have to say. Yeah give it a try. It's pretty good.

I buy this from sale and for price so low this was very good game. Calming to look and puzzles fun enough. I would not have want to pay any more then I did on sale because game is very short. When you got hold of how puzzles work game was quickly over and there is no many point to replay this. Buy it when on sale but don't spent too much money on it!

Nothing is explained, not even the puzzles. When the puzzles start there is a piece of paper at the side in which the desired outcome is drawn, or the mechanism, but in some cases you understand, in some cases you don't, and you just stare at that paper and think: "ok, what does this mean?".

The ending is dissappointing. Music also.
I suggest looking elsewhere for a good, satisfying adventure game .

This is one of the best hidden objects game that I ever played. Everything is so beautiful, the colors, the soundtracks, the graphics, the characters, everything!

The Tiny Bang Story is a cute point-and-click puzzle game about trying to repair a little planet that got broken into tiny puzzle pieces by a meteor. I really like that you can see all the areas you are about to explore on the main menu screen. 

You work through the five chapters solving different puzzles and mini-games. Most of them are pretty easy, though there's a hint system if you need it. There's no talking or text, instead the story comes through the artwork and music. Both are really well done. The art style is really whimsical with the tiny houses made out of everyday objects, like the house in the teapot. It fits really well together with the calm soundtrack.

I had a great time with it. The entire game took me about four hours to complete.

Short (around 2h - 2.5h) hidden object game. I liked the graphic, puzzles weren't hard but some of the objects were very well hidden. I enjoyed the game. Minigames and jigsaws <3

Incredibly charming art, but it boiled down to a bog standard point & click without a story to support it. 

Alt-tabbing while full-screened bricked my computer until I restarted it. That's a major, very fixable, issue and prompted an immediate uninstall. That it hasn't been fixed in all the time this game has been out is concerning.

"The Tiny Bang Story" est  un jeu qui s'adresse à tous : quel que soit l'âge, l'habitude de jeu, les possibilités matérielles, la maturité et la patience du joueur. L'originalité de ce titre, la grande diversité des challenges, la beauté des lieux, la poésie qui émane de TTBS font de ce jeu l'une des meilleures surprises de l'année selon moi. Malgré la durée de vie un peu courte (entre 3 et 5 heures environ) "The Tiny Bang Story" laisse un goût de rêve, et l'on se prend à attendre avec grande impatience le prochain titre réalisé par ceux qui nous ont fait goûter à ce petit morceau de paradis.

absolutely not worth full price, you *need* to buy on a sale, that being said, its a fun little game from childhood, worth checking out. not super long unfortunately and the ending is...less than satisfactory but still a fun game.
A variety of point-and-click puzzles in cute settings. The artwork and puzzles themselves make up for the fact that there is little-to-no plot. Well put-together. Not very long though.

This is not a game to get tense. This is not a game to be stressed. This is not a game to rush This is a game to relax, calm, and breath.

Go back to those days of playing I Spy or Where's Waldo from those books mixxed with hide and seek with items and a bit of camouflage as well. Then put in a few puzzles into the mix to spice it up.

The full price is worth it.

Only issue I had was that I couldn't get the intro to play again... only once when I tried the demo few months back. There is one puzzle that is more trivial than the others that it feels a bit annoying to solve.

A game in the vein of "Tiny Robots" or "Tiny Rooms", comprised of searches for needed objects to advance, accompanied by jigsaw puzzles, plumbing puzzles, mechanical construction, space invaders-like arcade games, etc.  In other words, an assortment of things to do, all in a colorfully cartoonish environment. What an absolute tragedy this game is. The game itself, phenomenal. But, and this is a BIG BUT, it is fundamentally BROKEN.

It's a hidden object / puzzle game that lets you proceed through the game without finding all the objects or solving the puzzles correctly. That'd be like playing Super Mario and when you fall in a pit, instead of dying, the game just warps you to the flagpole. Whoever ported this game from whatever platform it came from did an absolute trash job at QA.

Which is a shame, because I genuinely LOVED this game. And I don't even typically like this genre but what a masterpiece. It's just hard enough to give you a challenge, but easy enough that you can get through it. The music is chill. It's a nice little cozy casual game to relax with. And for the most part, the puzzles make sense. 

This is a problem I often have with puzzle games in that the author has chosen an obscure "method" to solve. Which usually makes no sense and you don't eve really figure it out, you just fumble your way through it or brute force it to pass. This game only had 1 or 2 of those, for the most part everything was pretty straightforward. Not easy, it took some thinking, but made sense.

If you're like me and you want your work to count for something, i.e. solving puzzles correctly and finding everything correctly, make a backup of your game save between every level. That way if you get "warped" erroneously, you can restore a save and try again (as the game will not let you go back and re-do it). They're stored in your C drive at Users\username\AppData\Roaming\Colibri Games\The Tiny Bang Story.

I genuinely wish they had taken the time to make this game work correctly, then it would have been a strong recommend from me! As it sits, it's still playable and maybe most people wouldn't even care. But I don't like getting an A for F work, which is what this game does.

A nice, if unspectacular point and click, hidden object game. Throughout five chapters, each made up of about four screens filled with things to interact with, you'll click on various people or mechanisms to initiate quests to find some hidden items they require. Once found and brought back, it will typically trigger a mini puzzle of some kind and give you another item upon completion that'll help you progress further. That's basically the long and short of it.

There is some kind of story about a meteor hitting "Tiny Planet" and scattering the world apart in the form of jigsaw pieces which are hidden all over the place, but it's largely inconsequential and serves only to back up a puzzle mechanic and explain how you access each chapter in turn (even though the jigsaw pieces aren't actually necessary to move on). There also seems to be a recurring character that appears in paintings and photographs showing him at different stages as he grows up, but the significance of this is never explained. Presumably we're retracing his steps in places that either he had an impact on, or which had an impact on him. It's hard to tell, and to be perfectly honest, even harder to care, since this is never expanded upon in any meaningful way or as any clear goal for the player.

Most of the puzzles and hidden objects are pretty fun and fair deals, but occasionally there's the odd obscure one that will have you either losing all faith in humanity, or else looking up a guide. I'm also really not a fan of them messing with the scale of the hidden objects, like having large jigsaw pieces in one place, then other, much small ones in other places yet still at the same distance away from the camera perspective. More consistancy of scale with the objects would be appreciated.

You'll have a fun, if not somewhat forgettable, two or so hours with the game, and have the option to replay any puzzle when you reach the end... which is possibly the most anti-climactic end I've ever experienced in a game. But I'd still recommend it for anyone looking for a quick break through a visually pretty world with some fun and engaging puzzles.

In theory, "The Tiny Bang Story" is a Hidden Object Game (HOG).  In reality, it's not.  Yes.  There are teeny tiny little objects to be found throughout the game.  But, that's not what a HOG is.  It's not really that important since other things swamp my rating.  But, it's something to be aware of.  The big thing that hurts the game is that nothing (absolutely nothing) is explained.  We're dumped into a setting with no idea what we're supposed to do, how to do it, or why.  The next biggest issues is somewhat related:  once we figure out what we're doing, we get into mini-puzzles.  But, once again, we're given no idea what to do with them.  Most of them can be figured out with the hint they give us.  But, some of them remain entirely opaque (I finished several by blindly flailing around with the mouse and never understood what I'd done to "succeed").  Next, as we move around the screen looking for those hidden objects or the secret areas they might be in, the cursor doesn't change to indicate any "hot" zones.  Basically, the game turns into a click-fest because we have to click on every single thing we see in case it's important.  And finally, the puzzles and objects aren't necessarily "necessary" to the game.  In the second area, I skipped a puzzle so I could come back to it later.  I ended up brute-forcing another puzzle which, I think, the puzzle I skipped was supposed to open.  The game happily let me do this and leave the area without ever finishing that puzzle.  In the third area, I finished the last puzzle before gathering the last hidden puzzle piece.  When I placed the object from that last puzzle where it belonged, the game happily moved me from the area and gave me all the puzzle pieces I needed for the world-puzzle.

I got 4.0 hours of game-play out of this.  So, the list price is a bit high purely from a dollar-per-hour aspect.  But, even if the game were much cheaper (heck, I paid 50 cents for it), the issues I noted above just put the game into the Not-Recommended area.

This is a fun, unique point-and-click puzzle/ hidden-object game. The game play, art, and music reminded me of the popular Machinarium, only the game is half as long in comparison. The puzzles were challenging and the hidden objects were hard to find. Additionally, the art was quirky and the music was strangely calming. I recommend this game if you're a fan of the Amanita franchise.

A relaxing, casual, hidden-object puzzler suitable for family fun.

8.5/10

[b][u]Pros:[/u][/b]
+ Very mellow, relaxing soundtrack
+ 5 zones of hidden objects and a variety of other puzzles including jigsaw puzzles, logic puzzles, easy arcade sequences etc.
+ Charming graphics
+ No speech or text, making this game universally understood

[b][u]Cons:[/u][/b]
- No zoom feature for smaller monitors, making it harder to spot hidden objects
- Each zone requires you to collect a certain number of jigsaw pieces, but you don't need to collect all of them to progress, making them feel a bit pointless
- Some puzzles are a bit obscure, frustrating or have "cheaty" solutions. Luckily there are walkthroughs online if you get stuck
- Quite a short game
